messages:
Sam R: Heads-up: we're rolling a tighter VPC egress policy into eu-west-1 tonight 22:00 UTC. This will DENY outbound 0.0.0.0/0 from the warm-pool subnets unless explicitly allowed. Expect new GPU node provisioning to fail with keystore/KMS egress blocked if we don't carve out access.

Priya K: @Sam R ack. Last time similar change spiked cold-starts by ~18%. Can we exempt the warm-pool subnet or open only privatelink to keystore? :thinking_face:

Sam R: Plan A is a privatelink exception: allow traffic to keystore.vpc.internal:443 and keystore-metrics:9090. Terraform change is ready in https://git.redwoodinfra/infra/vpc/commit/fea1c2. Deploy bot: `apply` scheduled at 22:00.

deploy-bot: plan applied to staging (tf-staging), no diffs. prod apply queued for 22:00 UTC.

Ben L: Important callout — we've tightened KMS key policy to use role-bound access (deploy role only). If bootstrap uses instance profile that doesn't have the new kms:Decrypt via new alias, decryption will fail during node init. Suggest adding a short-lived fallback alias mapping during rotation window.

Maria G: If we open privatelink, NATGW egress cost stays 0 for keystore, but setting up region relay (privatelink -> keystore) adds ENI cost. Tradeoff: NATGW per-GB vs ENI steady-state. I ran numbers: 10TB/month through NATGW = ~$950, ENI+NLB relay ~ $260/month + ~2-3% request overhead.

Priya K: Given cost, prefer privatelink carveout + regional relay for burst traffic. Can we also add a short-term iam segmentation: warm-pool nodes get a "bootstrap-decrypt" role with only current key aliases, and a canary env uses rotation key to validate?

Sam R: Yep. Proposed rollout steps: 1) Apply privatelink exception to warm-pool subnets (canary subset of nodes). 2) Create alias mapping and grant decrypt to "bootstrap-decrypt" role. 3) Canary create GPU node and run `node-bootstrap --debug` to verify keystore decrypt + docker pull. 4) Monitor provisioning latency/failed_attempts metric for 60m, fallback remove exception if >5% failure.

Ben L: Add an automated check in node-init: if KMS decrypt fails, fallback to retrieving from local vault-cache for up to 5 minutes while requeueing decrypt attempt. I'll open a small PR to the agent. Snippet:

```:
# node-init pseudocode
try:
  creds = kms.decrypt(alias=current_alias, ciphertext=env.SECRET)
except KMSDecryptError:
  creds = vault_cache.get('bootstrap-creds')
  metrics.incr('bootstrap.kms_fallback')
```

Maria G: Ops alert routing: route any provisioning failures to eng-sre and tag with `vpc-egress-rollout`. Also schedule a cost review next week if we keep privatelink carved out beyond the rollout window.

Priya K: Quick verification commands before rollout: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=warm --watch` and `curl -v https://keystore.vpc.internal:443/health` from a canary node. If TLS handshake fails, likely sg/privatelink ACL.

Sam R: I'll kick the prod apply and post back with canary node id. If anyone sees unexplained `InstanceProfile:AccessDenied` logs in cloud-init, ping me immediately.

deploy-bot: prod apply started at 22:00:12 UTC (run id: r-20260321-1).

Sam R: Canary node i-0ab12cd34ef567890 provisioned, node-init passed KMS decrypt and docker pulls. Observed provisioning time ~ 85s (baseline ~60s). Warmed up 2/5 nodes so far.

Priya K: Good. Keep an eye on failed_provision_count metric. If it creeps above 3% escalate to full rollback. :thumbsup:

Ben L: Follow-up: I'll merge the node-init fallback PR and add instrumentation to track fallback hits so we know if rotation windows are tight.

Maria G: Cost note logged in #finance: `privatelink-burst-relay` ticket with estimated monthly run-rate.

Sam R: Closing loop: rollout remains in exception state for 48h. After that we'll rotate keys and test alias migration, then remove exception if no regressions. Thanks all.
